summary:
Source-only research product closing a third suspicion (FileSnapshotStore.List aliasing) with the toolchain limit stated; preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics. No map change is proposed, so the accepted map and every accepted result keep their basis.

What was checked: List builds its result with `for _, meta := range snapshots { snapMeta = append(snapMeta, &meta.SnapshotMeta) }` (file_snapshot.go:226-242) over the pointers from getSnapshots (file_snapshot.go:244-289). That is the classic aliasing shape — every appended pointer would address the same range variable — and this module's go.mod declares go 1.20, below the version where per-iteration loop variables became the language default. A local run in a copy of the captured module created three snapshots and listed them: the entries came back distinct and correctly ordered (index 3, then 2, then 1), so the suspicion is excluded for this toolchain and module combination. The run is construction knowledge, not retained evidence — no controller execution was performed for it, and that limit is recorded explicitly along with the fact that builds with different loop-variable semantics are not covered.

New sources recorded: S62 (List) and S63 (getSnapshots). The feedback references existing objects only, so no new graph objects or versions were invented.

Frontier left open: the deployment-level premises behind the four confirmed findings (reachability of an unconfigured TimeoutNow sender, the election consequence of a fast-path heartbeat, whether batching FSMs are exempt from ConfigurationStore, and the lifetime of a snapshot-installed tail under a live leader); the ReloadConfig lease-timer lead; the processHeartbeat concurrency contract; and the still-unread observer plumbing, in-memory snapshot store, and net_transport beyond the heartbeat classification.
